profile.reading:
This record's address, 4421 29th Avenue Southeast, sits in Lowell, a small, historically industrial neighborhood in south Everett, Washington, on a bend of the Snohomish River. Lowell has long housed a mix of light-industrial, warehouse, and utility uses; the surrounding area sits within a few miles of Boeing's Everett assembly plant and Paine Field, part of the aerospace-and-technology corridor that runs through Snohomish County north of Seattle. That regional context, power infrastructure and industrial land built up around the aerospace industry, is plausibly why a small facility in Lowell would be mapped as a data center, but it does not, on its own, establish what actually operates at this specific address.

The name on file for this facility, "4421.io," does not resolve to any identifiable data center company. The domain currently points to Cascadia, an unrelated interactive climate and weather visualization tool for the Pacific Northwest, with no reference to Snohomish County, a physical facility, or a hosting business of any kind. No independent news coverage, trade-press mention, or business registration under the name "4421.io" describing a data center operator was found. It is possible the domain is simply a numeric address-based label assigned by whoever mapped the site rather than an actual company name, that it refers to a lapsed or repurposed domain unrelated to the facility's current use, or that this is a small-scale, non-public operation (a private server closet, a telecom equipment hut, or similar) that was tagged as a "data center" without a verifiable corresponding public entity.

For a public registry, that is itself useful information: not every mapped data center corresponds to a company that maintains a public identity or an active web presence, and a numeric or auto-generated-looking name attached to a residential-scale address in a mixed-use industrial neighborhood is a signal worth flagging rather than glossing over. Nothing here should be read as confirmation that a functioning data center of any meaningful scale exists at this address; equally, nothing here rules it out. Readers who have direct knowledge of what operates at 4421 29th Avenue Southeast in Everett are better positioned to clarify this record than any public search of the name currently attached to it. Until a legitimate operator can be identified, no power, capacity, tenancy, or construction details can be responsibly reported for this site.

reading.body:
This record is a false positive. There is no company called 4421.io, no corporate registration under that name, and no data center at these coordinates.

The single facility record originated in OpenStreetMap on August 10, 2026, when a mapper tagged coordinates in Lowell, Everett, Washington with the operator name 4421.io and the telecom tag set to data center. The coordinates fall directly on a two-story detached house at 4421 29th Avenue Southeast, mapped as a residential building two years earlier. The operator name is the street address with a .io suffix appended. The domain 4421.io is real and in active use, but it resolves to a personal weather and climate visualization tool for the Pacific Northwest running behind consumer-grade hosting, not a data center operation.

This failure mode recurs because OpenStreetMap's telecom tag carries no evidence requirement. Any mapper can attach it to any location for any reason, including labeling their own house with the domain they run from it. A registry that ingests these tags without verifying what the coordinates actually land on will report a single-family home as a facility and a personal domain as an operator, inflating both facility and operator counts. The absence of fields on this row, operator type, headquarters, website, and capacity, is itself the warning signal.

This row is retained rather than deleted so that anyone encountering the same tag in the same source can see it has been checked and what the answer was.
